dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts veterans receiving health care through the Department of Veterans Affairs who are furnished opioid antagonists.
dimensions.evidence: direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to furnish an opioid antagonist to a veteran without requiring a prescription or copayment.

dimensions.assessment: Removes administrative barriers (prescriptions and copayments) for veterans accessing life-saving opioid reversal medication.
dimensions.evidence: furnish an opioid antagonist to a veteran without requiring a prescription

dimensions.assessment: Eliminates copayments for veterans and places a mandate on the VA to furnish the medication, though no specific fiscal expenditure amount is stated.
dimensions.evidence: Elimination of Copayment.--Section 1722A of such title is amended, in subsection (a)(4), by striking all that follows 'veteran' and inserting a period.

dimensions.assessment: Amends title 38, United States Code, by creating a specific statutory requirement for the VA regarding a single class of medication.
dimensions.evidence: Subchapter II of chapter 17 of title 38, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section... 'Sec. 1720M. Opioid antagonists.'

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change to veterans' health care benefit rules regarding prescriptions and copayments.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall furnish an opioid antagonist to a veteran without requiring a prescription.

missing_information: Estimated cost to the federal government for supplying opioid antagonists without copayments or prescriptions.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to provide an opioid antagonist to veterans without requiring a prescription or copayment.
